description: Improve the cloud/local provider base_url UX so users stop pasting web/session URLs (the generic-openai-cloud Kiro session URL and the generic-openai-local Gemini generateContent URL), and add ADVISORY (not overly strict) validation that warns when a generic OpenAI-compatible base_url does not look like an API root. Frontend + a small advisory-only backend check. This depends on FEAT-001 only insofar as the surfaced enumeration error (a 404/HTML-not-JSON Decode error) now makes the cause visible; the UX changes here are otherwise independent. Every vitest that mounts App/Settings/ProviderKeysSection/LocalRuntimesSection/DiagnosticsSection/model-selector MUST mock invoke for ALL commands it calls with well-formed shapes; update mocks if any boundary shape changes.
steps: In hybrid-orchestrator/frontend/src/features/settings/ProviderKeysSection.tsx: improve the Kiro/genericOpenAI Base URL field. Add a clear label already present ('Base URL') plus a better placeholder and inline help text: e.g. placeholder 'https://host/v1' and a small helper line 'Enter the OpenAI-compatible API base URL, e.g. https://host/v1 - not a web or session URL.' Keep the existing required-when-genericOpenAI behavior. Add a lightweight client-side ADVISORY check (non-blocking): if the entered base URL contains '/session/' or ends with ':generateContent' or otherwise looks like a full endpoint/web URL rather than an API root, show a non-blocking advisory (role=status, reuse the existing warning region pattern, distinct from the blocking error region) telling the user it looks like a web/session URL and to use an OpenAI-compatible API base (e.g. https://host/v1). Do NOT block the save on this advisory (the backend remains the enforcement point; this is guidance). Consider clarifying the 'Kiro (OpenAI-compatible)' label copy so users understand it expects an API base URL. Do NOT hard-code any Kiro-specific endpoint.

In hybrid-orchestrator/frontend/src/features/settings/LocalRuntimesSection.tsx: apply the same base_url guidance to the generic OpenAI-compatible LOCAL runtime field - clearer placeholder and inline help ('OpenAI-compatible API base URL, e.g. http://localhost:1234/v1 - not a full model/generateContent URL') and the same non-blocking advisory when the entered URL contains '/session/' or ':generateContent' or a Gemini generativelanguage host. Add a gentle hint that Gemini should be configured via the Gemini KIND (Providers & Keys), not the generic OpenAI-compatible runtime. Keep existing behavior otherwise.

In crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs: add an ADVISORY (not blocking) base_url shape check for the GenericOpenAI kind on the write path. Extend the existing check_provider_base_url / validate_base_url flow so that when the kind is GenericOpenAI and the URL path contains '/session/' or ends with ':generateContent' (i.e. clearly not an API root), it produces an ADDITIONAL display-safe advisory string carried back in the CloudProviderConfigView.warning / LocalRuntimeConfigView.warning - WITHOUT blocking the save (do not turn it into a Blocked verdict; only link-local/metadata IPs remain blocked). If wiring this into validate_base_url is awkward because it lacks the kind, add a small separate helper `advise_generic_openai_base_url(url: &str) -> Option<String>` called from set_cloud_provider_inner / set_local_runtime_inner for the GenericOpenAI kind and merge its message with any existing plaintext-TLS warning. Keep it advisory and narrow.

Update TS types if any boundary shape changed: if FEAT-001 or step 3 changed no serde struct field, frontend/src/types/index.ts needs no change. If the warning field semantics are unchanged (still string|null), leave the types as-is. Verify ProviderDiagnostic/ProviderEnumerationError/CloudProviderConfig/LocalRuntimeConfig TS mirrors still match the Rust structs exactly (camelCase).

Update/extend vitest mocks and tests in hybrid-orchestrator/frontend/src/features/settings/settings.test.tsx (and any other test mounting the changed components): add a test that entering a '/session/' or ':generateContent' style base URL for the Kiro/genericOpenAI provider shows the non-blocking advisory (role=status) and still allows saving (invoke set_cloud_provider is called). Add a parallel test for the local generic OpenAI-compatible runtime. Ensure the invoke mock returns well-formed CloudProviderConfig/LocalRuntimeConfig shapes (id/kind/baseUrl/hasApiKey/warning) and that list_cloud_providers/list_local_runtimes/list_available_models/provider_diagnostics mocks are present for any mounted component. If step 3 makes the backend attach an advisory warning for such URLs, assert the returned config.warning surfaces in the warning region too.

Add a Rust test in commands.rs #[cfg(test)] for the advisory: set_cloud_provider_inner with kind GenericOpenAI and a base_url like 'https://app.kiro.dev/session/abc' succeeds (row is persisted, NOT blocked) and returns a CloudProviderConfigView whose warning mentions it looks like a web/session URL; and a base_url like 'https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-flash-latest:generateContent' (local path via set_local_runtime_inner or cloud) also succeeds with an advisory. Assert a normal 'https://host/v1' yields no such advisory. Keep the existing blocked-internal-host tests passing (link-local still blocks).

Run `NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` in hybrid-orchestrator/frontend IF a prettier binary is already installed offline; otherwise hand-verify formatting and note it. Run `cargo fmt --manifest-path hybrid-orchestrator/crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml --check` if rustfmt is available.

Self-audit: TS eslint no-unused-vars (remove any unused imports/vars from the new advisory logic), tsc strict (no implicit any; the advisory helper returns string | null). Rust clippy -D warnings clean for the new helper (no unused, no needless_lifetimes).
acceptance_criteria: The Kiro/genericOpenAI Base URL field (Providers & Keys) has a clear label, an informative placeholder, and inline help stating it must be an OpenAI-compatible API base URL (e.g. https://host/v1), not a web/session URL.
The generic OpenAI-compatible LOCAL runtime field has the same guidance and a hint to configure Gemini via the Gemini kind.

Entering a '/session/'-style or ':generateContent'-style URL shows a NON-BLOCKING advisory (does not prevent saving); the backend still persists the row and the surfaced enumeration error (from FEAT-001) explains an unusable endpoint.

The backend attaches a display-safe advisory warning for a GenericOpenAI base_url that clearly is not an API root ('/session/' or ':generateContent'), without blocking the save; link-local/metadata IPs remain the only blocked case.
No hard-coded Kiro endpoint is introduced; the generic path stays a generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
All vitest suites mounting the changed components mock invoke for every command they call with well-formed shapes; new tests assert the advisory behavior; the suite is structurally correct.
verification: OFFLINE: npm/vitest cannot install (npm 403); verify by reading the tests to confirm the advisory assertions and that all invoke calls are mocked with correct shapes.
OFFLINE (if prettier binary present): `NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` in frontend; (if rustfmt present) cargo fmt --check for tauri-app.
CI (authoritative): frontend eslint + tsc + `npm test` (vitest) pass; the tauri-app per-crate cargo test/clippy pass with the new advisory test.
